name: HEPCAT
title: HEPCAT: High Energy Physics Constructive Amplitude Tool
summary: Build, simplify, complete and validate scattering amplitudes with explicit spinor identities.
paragraphs: HEPCAT helps you derive scattering amplitudes using spinor identities, constructive diagrams and factorization. You can start with an expression you already have, work through individual diagrams, or ask [ConstructAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ConstructAmplitude) to carry out the supported construction workflow. If this is your first visit, begin with [Getting Started](paclet:HEPCAT/tutorial/GettingStarted).

A process is an ordered list such as `{"e", "E", "A.+", "A.+"}`. The positions in that list give the particle labels in the resulting formula. All analytic momenta are incoming. You choose the physical incoming and outgoing states later, when exporting a numerical process.

The model is an explicit input to each calculation. [ReadModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReadModel) loads particle properties, interactions and numerical parameter values into one model object. A diagram model contains the elementary interactions. A factorization model must also contain the complete lower-point amplitudes needed to test the process you are constructing. Keeping these two roles distinct is particularly important above four points.

For a guided calculation, generate diagrams with [CreateDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateDiagrams), convert them with [DiagramAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/DiagramAmplitudes), and simplify them with [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes). [CompleteFactorization](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteFactorization) and [CompleteHighEnergy](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteHighEnergy) then try to repair the remaining discrepancies. The [staged construction tutorial](paclet:HEPCAT/tutorial/ConstructingAndCheckingAnAmplitude) explains what each step receives and returns.

Use [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes) to inspect a proposed result. Its report separates physical residues, apparent spurious poles, high-energy behavior and explicit reference-spinor dependence. A numerical PASS is evidence from the tested configurations; an unresolved check remains visible. For a finished symbolic result, [WriteSPINASProcess](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/WriteSPINASProcess) creates numerical C++ code and can connect it to independent CalcHEP and MadGraph checks.

name: SpinorAlgebra
title: Spinors, Momenta and Spin Sums
summary: Represent and manipulate angle brackets, square brackets, momentum chains and spin indices.
paragraphs: A bracket such as an angle or square product is represented by [SpinorChain](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorChain), with [Spinor](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Spinor) objects at its ends. Put [Mom](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/Mom) objects between the endpoints for momentum insertions. The notebook display gives the familiar bracket notation while retaining an expression that the algebra functions can manipulate.

Particle labels and spin indices play different roles. A label identifies which external momentum belongs to a factor; an explicit massive-spin index selects a component. [ChooseSpinIndices](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ChooseSpinIndices) makes spin choices, whereas [PermuteParticles](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PermuteParticles) relabels the particles throughout the expression. [ReverseMomentum](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReverseMomentum) implements crossing, including the associated spinor signs.

Start with [ReduceSpinContractions](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinContractions) when contracted spin indices remain, and [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts) for ordinary chain identities. Neither is a substitute for supplying the complete process and diagram-local assumptions to [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes). The [identity tutorial](paclet:HEPCAT/tutorial/ApplyingSpinorIdentities) shows how to inspect individual exact moves.

name: ModelsAndParameters
title: Models and Model-Local Parameters
summary: Read model tables, retrieve known amplitudes and save new results.
paragraphs: Use [ReadModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReadModel) as the entry point for a model directory. It reads the related model tables together, resolves their parameter names consistently, and returns an object that you pass to subsequent functions. The component-file readers are implementation details of that operation.

You can keep several models in one Mathematica session. A parameter such as the electron mass belongs to its model; loading a second model does not overwrite a global electron-mass value. [ModelParameter](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameter), [ModelFunction](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelFunction) and [ModelParameterRules](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameterRules) let you inspect those symbolic quantities and their numerical assignments.

The distinction between an interaction and a complete amplitude matters. Use elementary interactions for [CreateDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateDiagrams). Use complete known amplitudes for [FactorizationAmplitudeChannels](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FactorizationAmplitudeChannels). For example, a five-point factorization channel can require a known four-point amplitude, even though the five-point diagrams are built from three-point vertices.

After obtaining and checking a new result, [AppendModelAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/AppendModelAmplitudes) can write it to the factorization model for a later higher-point calculation. Check the particle order, helicities and overall sign before saving. [LookupAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/LookupAmplitude) retrieves a stored expression for inspection or export.

sections.title: Parameters Stay with Their Model
sections.description: Inspect or override numerical assignments without replacing symbolic masses and couplings throughout the notebook.

name: DiagramsAndFactorization
title: Diagrams and Factorization Channels
summary: Generate diagrams and physical channel expressions from model data.
paragraphs: Diagrams and factorization channels describe the same process in different ways. [CreateDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateDiagrams) enumerates the tree diagrams allowed by the supplied interaction model. [CreateArrowDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateArrowDiagrams) shows their topology and particle flow, and [DiagramAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/DiagramAmplitudes) converts the complete list to algebraic expressions.

The amplitude converter returns one `{massRules, expression}` pair for each diagram. The mass rules identify the known external masses and the internal channels associated with that particular constructive diagram. Keep each pair together until preparation is complete. Summing the expressions first would lose the association between a numerator and its allowed internal on-shell conditions.

[FactorizationAmplitudeChannels](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FactorizationAmplitudeChannels) instead starts from complete known lower-point amplitudes. Each returned channel identifies the momentum that goes on shell and gives the sewn product divided by its propagator denominator. Those channel expressions are the targets for [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes) and [CompleteFactorization](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteFactorization).

For a Feynman model, the same diagram entry points return ordinary off-shell internal tensors. [FeynmanToSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FeynmanToSpinorProducts) converts supported tensors to the spinor notation. This provides an independent comparison rather than a new source of constructive internal-shell assumptions.

name: IdentitiesAndSimplification
title: Identities and Simplification
summary: Apply exact identities and inspect legal one-step rewrites.
paragraphs: There are three useful levels of simplification. [ReduceSpinContractions](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinContractions) removes contracted spin indices. [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts) applies ordinary chain and external on-shell identities. [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) also knows the process, the supplied mass rules and the reference-spinor prescription, so it can make more informed choices.

When you want to understand a derivation, use [SpinorIdentityCandidates](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorIdentityCandidates) to inspect legal edits and [ApplySpinorIdentity](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ApplySpinorIdentity) to replay one. This keeps the identity route explicit instead of treating a large simplification as one unexplained operation. [SpinorExpressionComplexity](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorExpressionComplexity) gives a consistent measure for comparing intermediate forms.

Apply numerator-specific rules with [ApplyToNumerator](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ApplyToNumerator). It works on the terms as they stand: it does not expand a factored numerator or combine different denominators. Internal on-shell conditions belong only to the individual constructive numerator for which they were supplied. They must not be imposed on a complete final amplitude or on its physical propagator denominators.

A shorter expression is not automatically a physically correct one. After combining diagrams or adding corrections, use [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes). The [kinematics tutorial](paclet:HEPCAT/tutorial/KinematicsAndOnShellConditions) explains which assumptions remain valid at each stage.

name: AmplitudeConstruction
title: Constructing and Completing Amplitudes
summary: Prepare diagram seeds, solve factorization constraints and complete allowed high-energy behavior.
paragraphs: [ConstructAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ConstructAmplitude) is the normal starting point when you want a complete supported amplitude rather than an isolated symbolic reduction. Give it the ordered process, an interaction model for diagrams and a model containing the known lower-point amplitudes for factorization. It reports the stage being performed and the elapsed time.

The stages are also available separately. [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) simplifies the starting diagram expressions. [CompleteFactorization](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteFactorization) tries corrections constrained by the physical channel residues. [CompleteHighEnergy](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteHighEnergy) uses the remaining allowed freedom to address the high-energy conditions while retaining the other constraints.

For an ordinary calculation, start with the defaults. Set `"PolePreference"` when you want to favor a form with physical or spurious reference poles. A preference guides the search; the final checks still decide whether the proposed result is acceptable. A clock, an insufficient correction space or an unresolved comparison can prevent completion, and the function reports that rather than returning an unchecked result as a success.

If you supply an independent `"FeynmanModel"`, [ConstructAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ConstructAmplitude) can validate one fixed constructive representative even when proving every remaining affine-family identity is unfinished. All standard checks and the Feynman comparison must pass at the normal validation parameter assignments. The benchmark does not supply the answer or fit its coefficients. Details retain the family and state that uniqueness has not been established; direct [CompleteHighEnergy](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteHighEnergy) calls keep their strict completion semantics.

If a construction fails, repeat the relevant stage with its detailed output and inspect the failing channels or unresolved checks. The [staged tutorial](paclet:HEPCAT/tutorial/ConstructingAndCheckingAnAmplitude) provides a calculation you can follow without hiding the intermediate amplitudes.

name: AmplitudeValidation
title: Checking Amplitudes
summary: Compare physical residues, spurious poles, high-energy behavior, references and Feynman results.
paragraphs: [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes) answers a practical question: is this proposed amplitude consistent with the supplied lower-point amplitudes and the expected behavior of the complete process? Its compact table is intended to be read first. Request more detail only for a comparison that you want to investigate.

Physical-pole checks compare the residue of the complete expression with the product specified by each factorization channel. Apparent poles in the formula that are absent from the supplied physical channels are examined as possible spurious poles. High-energy and explicit reference-spinor checks test different properties and are reported separately. Passing one kind of check does not replace the others.

Use `"Output" -> "Residues"` to see the compared samples, or `"Output" -> "Details"` for the complete diagnostic record. `"Opp Sign"` is useful information: it means the comparison has the opposite overall sign at the tested samples. An unresolved result means that the check did not establish its conclusion within its supported method or resource limit.

The numerical choices come from the model by default. An explicit random seed makes a run repeatable; it does not make a sampled check an analytic proof. For an independent benchmark, supply compatible Feynman amplitudes, or export numerical code and use [ValidateMadGraph](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ValidateMadGraph) and the CalcHEP comparison provided by [WriteSPINASProcess](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/WriteSPINASProcess).

name: FeynmanAmplitudes
title: Feynman Models and Spinor Conversion
summary: Use CalcHEP Feynman rules as an independent off-shell diagram backend.
paragraphs: [ReadModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReadModel) recognizes supported CalcHEP model tables and returns a [FeynmanModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FeynmanModel). You can then use the familiar [CreateDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateDiagrams) and [DiagramAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/DiagramAmplitudes) functions. The model selects the interpretation of the vertices and propagators.

The first algebraic result uses Dirac chains, Lorentz tensors and polarization vectors. [FeynmanToSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FeynmanToSpinorProducts) converts supported objects to HEPCAT spinor products using the package conventions. The tensor-head reference pages below explain how to read an expression; most users do not need to construct those objects by hand.

Feynman internal momenta remain off shell in the numerator as well as the denominator. This is essential for an independent comparison with a completed constructive result. [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) recognizes that distinction and uses a shared reference choice across the Feynman diagrams.

The [Feynman comparison tutorial](paclet:HEPCAT/tutorial/FeynmanComparison) walks from a model through conversion and preparation to a combined validation report. Unsupported tensors or external states remain explicit rather than being silently dropped.

name: FormattingAndExport
title: Formatting, Model Output and SPINAS Export
summary: Display analytic expressions and write numerical C++ processes.
paragraphs: Choose an output tool according to what you want to do with the expression. [PlainText](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PlainText) gives a readable text representation, including a model-file form for supported exact expressions. [TeX](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/TeX) writes mathematical LaTeX notation. [SPINAS](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SPINAS) is the older expression-level C++ formatter.

For a complete numerical process, use [WriteSPINASProcess](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/WriteSPINASProcess). It writes the process class, spin/helicity interface, build files, examples and optional validation backends together. Supply all analytic massless-helicity sectors needed by the physical process, or explicitly select the helicities that you want to retain.

Analytic expressions use all incoming momenta. The numerical exporter needs an explicit physical incoming-to-outgoing process, so it can cross the outgoing momenta and angle spinors exactly once. Do not manually cross a formula and then give it to an exporter that will cross it again.

The [SPINAS export tutorial](paclet:HEPCAT/tutorial/ExportingToSPINAS) covers source generation, compiling, independent comparisons and numerical event generation. Generated run directories live under the build directory by default. To store a new symbolic result for later factorization, use [AppendModelAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/AppendModelAmplitudes) rather than copying C++ output into a model file.

name: LegacyAmplitudeSearch
title: Reserved and Earlier APIs
summary: Recognize historical names and use the maintained calculation workflow.
paragraphs: Some names remain exported for compatibility with old notebooks but have no callable implementation on this branch. Their individual pages identify that status explicitly. A help page for a reserved name does not make the old algorithm available.
Use ConstructAmplitude and the exact identity tools for current constructive work. Machine-learning simplification and evolutionary amplitude-search development are not required by these tools.

name: ReferenceIndex
title: HEPCAT Reference Index
summary: Alphabetical reference for every documented public function and symbolic head.
paragraphs: This index lists the functions and symbolic objects intended for direct use in a HEPCAT calculation. Choose a name to see its calling form, an explanation of its inputs and result, examples and links to the surrounding workflow.

If you are deciding where to begin, use the [main guide](paclet:HEPCAT/guide/HEPCAT) or [Getting Started](paclet:HEPCAT/tutorial/GettingStarted). The alphabetical list is most useful once you know which operation you need.
